turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hey, Dr. Smith. Yeah, um... well, what really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. 

Like, I’ll be sitting at my workbench—I do custom jewelry and metalwork. Actually, the price of silver has been absolutely insane lately, you wouldn't believe the markups. I was telling my buddy Dave about it the other day, he runs a shop over on 4th street, and he was saying he might have to start using cheaper alloys. I think that's a terrible idea because it just doesn't polish the same way, you know? It gets this weird cloudy look if you don't buff it right. 

But anyway, yeah, at the bench, I’ll just jump from reading a customer email, to noticing a tiny saw mark on a ring I'm filing, to hearing a noise outside... like yesterday there was this loud truck, sounded like an old diesel. I used to mess around with engines back in high school so I always try to guess what kind of motor it is when I hear one drive by. And then I turn back around and I realize I’ve completely lost the whole work order I was supposed to be doing. It just keeps happening like that.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes an inability to sustain attention on their work, stating their mind won't stay on one thing and they lose track of their tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly notes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, such as hearing a noise outside from a truck.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's response demonstrates tangential speech, frequently going off-topic about silver prices, a friend's shop, and diesel engines before returning to the main point.
symptom_reasoning.S039: The patient reports that their attention is easily drawn to irrelevant external stimuli (like a truck outside) and describes frequent task switching and an inability to sustain attention.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any times in your life where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or productive for days at a time, to the point where you didn't feel like you needed much sleep?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually. Like right after this big jewelry show I did a few months back. I felt completely lit up, just... larger than life, you know? I was ready to take on the world. 

That show was out at the county expo center, which, by the way, they charge way too much for parking now. It used to be five bucks and now it's fifteen, and they don't even have security watching the lot. My buddy got his catalytic converter stolen there last year. It's crazy, you gotta be so careful where you park trucks these days, especially if you have any decent tools in the back. They can cut those things out in like two minutes flat with a Sawzall... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. After the show. Yeah, I was so pumped up, but then one minute I'm feeling invincible, and the next I'm just snapping at anyone who asked me to stick to normal shop hours or told me to slow down. It's like, why would I slow down? I'm in the zone! And they want me to just pack up and go home at 5 PM like some kind of bank teller. But yeah, the parking at that expo center is a total scam.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by unrelated thoughts about parking and catalytic converters, losing their original train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality, going off on a completely unrelated tangent about expo center parking and theft before catching themselves.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient describes feeling 'lit up' and 'larger than life,' followed by snapping at people, indicating both elevated and irritable mood.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient describes being 'in the zone' and refusing to slow down or stick to normal hours, indicating increased energy and activity.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient reports feeling 'invincible' and 'larger than life,' demonstrating inflated self-esteem and grandiosity.
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient admits to 'snapping at anyone' who asked them to stick to normal hours or slow down.

turns.doctor_question: During that time after the jewelry show when you felt 'lit up' and invincible, how many days in a row did that feeling last?
turns.patient_response:
Well, that whole wired, out-of-control stretch started right after they gave me this award at the show. It was for "Best Contemporary Metalwork" or something like that. They gave me this little glass plaque, which honestly, the engraving on it was pretty sloppy. You could tell they just ran it through a cheap laser engraver. If they had asked me, I could have hand-engraved it and made it look a hundred times better. Hand engraving is a dying art, really. Everyone just wants to use machines now because it's faster, but you lose that human touch, you know? It's like how people buy those mass-produced rings from the mall instead of getting something custom-made that actually has a soul to it. 

But yeah, anyway, the feeling lasted for about two weeks straight. Just two weeks of going a hundred miles an hour.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient confirms experiencing a two-week 'wired, out-of-control stretch,' indicating a distinct period of elevated mood.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient describes their energy during this two-week period as 'going a hundred miles an hour,' reflecting abnormally increased activity and energy.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient demonstrates inflated self-esteem and overestimation of abilities by claiming they could have hand-engraved the award 'a hundred times better' than the professionals.

turns.doctor_question: During those two weeks when you felt invincible and were going a hundred miles an hour, did you ever see or hear things that others didn't, or did you have any thoughts that were so intense that people around you thought they were strange or impossible?
turns.patient_response:
No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody said anything about my thoughts being impossible. I was just having really big ideas, you know? Like, I wanted to completely redesign my entire workshop layout. 

Which, actually, is something I've been meaning to do for a while because the ventilation in there is just terrible. When I'm soldering, especially with silver solder, the fumes can get pretty bad. You really need a good fume extractor, not just a fan blowing out the window. I was looking at this one model online, it's got a HEPA filter and everything, but the shipping cost was outrageous. It's coming from overseas, and ever since the supply chain got all messed up, getting anything heavy shipped is a nightmare. I remember ordering a new anvil a couple years ago, and it got stuck at the port for like three months. Three months! And when it finally arrived, the crate was all smashed up. Luckily, you can't really break an anvil, but still, it's the principle of the thing. If I'm paying for shipping, I expect the box to arrive in one piece. 

But no, no voices or seeing things or anything crazy like that. Just... just going fast.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having thoughts that others considered impossible or crazy.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or seeing things that others did not.

turns.doctor_question: During those two weeks, did your behavior or your 'big ideas' cause any major problems for you, such as getting you into trouble at work, causing you to lose your job, or leading to an emergency room visit?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I didn't go to the hospital or get fired, since I work for myself, but... yeah, it did cause some issues. I completely missed this major custom delivery. I was supposed to finish this set of wedding bands, and I just... I don't know, I got so caught up in redesigning the shop and starting all these new, massive projects that I totally blew past the deadline. 

Which is terrible for business, obviously. Word of mouth is everything in custom jewelry. If you screw up a wedding, people talk. It's not like buying a toaster where you just return it if it's broken. A wedding ring is, like, a symbol of eternity, you know? And speaking of eternity, the price of gold right now is just... it's astronomical. I remember when I first started apprenticing, gold was maybe a thousand an ounce, and now? You basically have to take out a mortgage just to cast a decent-sized pendant. And the suppliers, they nickel and dime you on everything. They charge you for the metal, the shipping, the insurance... and don't even get me started on the refining fees when you send your scrap sweeps in. They always claim your scrap is lower karat than it actually is. It's a racket, I swear. 

But anyway, yeah, the shop records got completely disorganized during that time, too. I had invoices mixed up with sketches, metal stock not logged... it was such a mess that I had to actually stop taking new work just to sort it out. I'm still trying to catch up. And my family, they've been calling and coming by the shop a lot more lately. I think they got pretty worried because I just stopped doing my normal routines, like eating regular meals or keeping the place clean. They keep asking if I'm okay, which is annoying, but I guess I get it. But man, those refining fees... total scam.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient failed to finish workplace duties, completely missing a major custom delivery deadline for a set of wedding bands.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states their shop records got completely disorganized, mixing up invoices with sketches and failing to log metal stock.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient stopped maintaining normal daily routines, such as eating regular meals and keeping their workspace clean.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and loose associations, drifting from the topic of wedding rings to eternity, gold prices, and refining fees.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes a surge in goal-directed activity, getting caught up in redesigning the shop and starting multiple new, massive projects.

turns.doctor_question: During those two weeks, did your behavior become so out of control that it was obvious to others that you were unable to function, or did it require you to have someone else step in to manage your daily life?
turns.patient_response:
Well, like I was saying, it definitely caused some major problems. I mean, missing that custom wedding band delivery was huge. I had to literally stop taking on any new commissions just to untangle the mess my shop records were in. I had invoices and design sketches just piled everywhere. 

Which reminds me, I really need to switch to a digital invoicing system. I've been doing it all on paper, and paper is just so unreliable. Plus, the price of printer ink? Don't even get me started. It's literally more expensive than human blood, ounce for ounce. I saw a documentary about that once. They were talking about how printer companies sell the printers at a loss just so they can gouge you on the cartridges. It's the same business model as razors and razor blades. You buy the handle for cheap, but then you're locked into buying their ridiculously overpriced blades for the rest of your life. I tried switching to a safety razor a few months ago to save money. You know, the old-school metal ones where you just replace the single blade? It's supposed to be better for your skin anyway, less irritation. But I ended up cutting my chin pretty bad the first time I used it. Still have a little scar right here. 

But yeah, I wasn't like, totally incapable of tying my shoes or anything, but my family definitely noticed I wasn't functioning right. They got really worried because I just dropped all my normal routines, and they've been checking in on me a lot more lately to make sure I'm actually eating and keeping things together. They mean well, but it's a lot.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient failed to complete a major workplace duty, missing a custom wedding band delivery.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes their shop records as a mess with invoices and sketches piled everywhere, indicating difficulty organizing tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from discussing shop records to printer ink prices, razor blades, and a shaving scar.

turns.doctor_question: During that two-week period, was your behavior ever so extreme that you had to be hospitalized or placed in a facility for your own safety?
turns.patient_response:
No, no hospitals. Like I said before, I didn't go to the hospital. I actually really hate hospitals, to be honest. The lighting in those places is just... it's so sterile and harsh. Those cheap fluorescent ceiling tubes. 

You know, fluorescent lighting is absolutely the worst possible environment for looking at gemstones. If you try to color-match sapphires or grade a diamond under that kind of light, you are going to completely mess up the piece. It washes all the depth out of the stone. You really need proper full-spectrum lighting, or better yet, natural daylight. I used to have this perfect natural light coming through the east window of my shop, right over my main bench. It was incredible for working with opals. But then the city—without even sending a letter, mind you—just showed up one morning with a backhoe and planted this massive elm tree right on the sidewalk. Just completely blocked my light. 

And the guys who planted it left dirt all over the pavement for a week. I had to go out there with a push broom myself because customers were tracking it into the shop. Mud and fine jewelry do not mix, let me tell you. It gets into the carpet and you can never get it out. I ended up having to rent one of those industrial carpet cleaners from the hardware store, the ones that weigh like eighty pounds. 

But... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, facilities. No, nothing like that. I just stayed at my house and the shop. Nobody locked me up anywhere.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality and derailment, wandering off-topic from hospitals to lighting, gemstones, a tree, and carpet cleaning before finally returning to the original question.

turns.doctor_question: During those two weeks, did your behavior cause a marked impairment in your social or occupational functioning, such as putting your business or relationships at significant risk, or was it just a noticeable change that others were concerned about?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I mean, I think I already touched on most of this, but it was definitely a major problem, not just a little change. Like I said, missing that major custom delivery was a huge hit, and my shop records got so incredibly disorganized that I've had to stop taking on any new work for now just to fix the mess. 

Which really hurts, because I actually had to turn away this lady on Tuesday who wanted a vintage platinum brooch repaired. And let me tell you, platinum is already a total nightmare to work with anyway. The melting point is insanely high compared to gold or silver. You have to use these special welding goggles, like a shade six lens, just so you don't burn your retinas out from the brightness of the torch. I actually knew a guy back when I was first learning who didn't wear his safety glasses once, and he had blind spots in his vision for a solid week. It's crazy that they just let a bunch of teenagers play with acetylene torches and boiling acid. We use this stuff called pickle—it's a mild acid compound for cleaning the metal after you solder it—and if you accidentally drop a piece of hot metal into the pickle pot, it splashes everywhere. I have ruined so many good shirts that way. You can always tell who a jeweler is by the tiny little acid burn holes in their jeans. I try to wear an apron now, but the straps always dig into my neck...

But, um... wait. Yeah, so work is basically on hold. And my family has been checking on me a lot more lately because they got really worried about how far I'd slipped from my usual routines. So, yeah, it definitely messed up my functioning pretty badly.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states that their shop records became so incredibly disorganized that they had to stop taking on new work.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality by going off on a long, loosely related tangent about platinum, welding goggles, and acid burns before catching themselves and returning to the original topic.
